Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said regarding the (animal) slaughtered without iron: 'When you are compelled to do so, and you do not find an iron, then slaughter it with a stone.'

key_terms.اضْطِرَار: Compulsion, necessity; the legal state of being forced by circumstances
key_terms.الذَّبِيحَة: Slaughtered animal; the act and object of ritual slaughter
key_terms.حَجَر: Stone; a permitted substitute for iron in cases of necessity
key_terms.حَدِيدَة: Iron implement; the standard blade required for lawful slaughter

ai.seo_question: Can you slaughter an animal with a stone if no iron is available in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) issued a legal ruling on emergency slaughter: if an iron blade cannot be found, slaughter with a sharp stone is permissible. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that necessity (idhtirar) can permit what is ordinarily required — i.e., the use of an iron blade for valid slaughter. The original audience, students of fiqh, would have understood this as an application of the necessity exception (darura) found throughout Islamic law.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said regarding the (animal) slaughtered without iron. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When you are desperate towards it, and you do not find an iron, so slaughter it by a stone’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “
About the case of slaughtering without iron, abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘In an emergency when you cannot find iron you can slaughter with stone.”’
